description.ncbi_summary: Aldehyde dehydrogenases oxidize various aldehydes to the corresponding acids. They are involved in the detoxification of alcohol-derived acetaldehyde and in the metabolism of corticosteroids, biogenic amines, neurotransmitters, and lipid peroxidation. The enzyme encoded by this gene forms a cytoplasmic homodimer that preferentially oxidizes aromatic and medium-chain (6 carbons or more) saturated and unsaturated aldehyde substrates. It is thought to promote resistance to UV and 4-hydroxy-2-nonenal-induced oxidative damage in the cornea. The gene is located within the Smith-Magenis syndrome region on chromosome 17. Multiple alternatively spliced variants, encoding the same protein, have been identified. [provided by RefSeq, Sep 2008].

uniprot_function.text: Cytosolic aldehyde dehydrogenase that catalyzes the oxidation of aldehydes to their corresponding carboxylic acids, preferentially using NAD+ but also accepting NADP+ as cofactor, with a strong preference for medium- and long-chain saturated and unsaturated aliphatic aldehydes (PubMed:12943535, PubMed:1737758, PubMed:36966166). In the corneal epithelium, contributes to protection against UV-induced oxidative damage by metabolizing toxic lipid peroxidation-derived aldehydes, including 4-hydroxy-2-nonenal (4-HNE) and malondialdehyde (PubMed:12706498, PubMed:17158879). In addition to its catalytic activity, functions as a corneal crystallin and constitutes a major fraction of the water-soluble protein content of the mammalian corneal epithelium (PubMed:12943535). Independently of catalysis, acts as a direct UV absorber, reducing UV-induced inactivation and aggregation of other corneal proteins through a competitive UV-filtering mechanism (PubMed:17158879). Also exhibits molecular chaperone-like activity in vitro, protecting proteins from thermal- and stress-induced aggregation and inactivation (PubMed:28526614). May contribute to the maintenance of corneal epithelial homeostasis through modulation of epithelial proliferation and differentiation programs (PubMed:26751691). Expressed in the nasal mucosa, displays enzymatic activity toward a variety of aldehyde odorant substrates in vitro and may contribute to odorant metabolism (PubMed:36966166).
